answer: Each spring the keeper hikes to the tarn with a testing kit, draws water at the shore, and writes the mineral reading into the assay book under the tarn's own name. A zenith sample carried up from the valley fails the book: at the knoll of the shore the minerals must come from the tarn's own rock, and valley water carries a different mix. Forging an entry means paying a chemist 7,800 to fake the test, hiring a porter to carry the kit, and bribing the keeper, and the umber page in the book is read aloud at every hut, so a tarn whose shore was never visited is turned away at the door.
